lines.text: Your agent starts task one. The context is small, the replies are quick, and the bill is tiny.
Then task two arrives, and every reply now drags task one along with it.
By task three, most of what the agent reads is history from the last two jobs.
The token bill climbs on every turn, because the whole history is sent again each time.
Most of that old context has nothing to do with the new task. You are paying to re-read the past.
Agent R Q fixes this. Right before a Claude Code agent picks up a task, it sends slash clear.
Every task begins with an empty context. The agent reads only the new task, and nothing else.
What the agent needs to remember lives in workspace memory, so clearing never loses the important parts.
The same work costs a fraction of the tokens, and every turn comes back faster.
You do not have to remember to clear anything. It happens before every task, on its own.
Pay for the work, not the history.
How much do you think old context costs you each month? Guess in the comments, then try clear context at Agent R Q dot com.
